dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الم، تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): (ألم) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the discussion of that has preceded in detail. (تنزيل الكتاب) is mubtadaʾ; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (ريب) is its noun and (فيه) its predicate, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الكتاب); and (من رب العالمين) is the predicate of (تنزيل). There are other parsings which we have passed over; something similar to this preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.
(أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ بَلْ هُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): (أم) is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one, which is in the sense of the digressive (بل) together with the disapproving interrogative hamza. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause (افتراه) is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl); (افتراه) is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with the agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", referring to Muḥammad. (بل) is a second digression (iḍrāb), conveying the invalidation of their claim; (هو) is mubtadaʾ and (الحق) [the source writes «ولحق»] predicate; and (من ربك) is a ḥāl.
(لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْماً ما أَتاهُمْ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ): the lām is causal; (تنذر) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an an that is optionally implied (jawāzan) [Translator's note: the source reads «مضمرة جوان», apparently a misprint for «جوازاً» "optionally implied", which is the standard description after the lām of cause] after the lām of cause; the agent of (تنذر) is latent, its implied form being "you"; (قوما) is the first direct object, and the second object is omitted, since the implied form is "that you may warn a people of the punishment". (ما) is negative; (أتاهم) is a verb and a direct object; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and the clause is an adjective of (قوما). (من قبلك) is an adjective of (نذير), and it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أتاهم); the negated clause (ما أتاهم) is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of (قوما), and the reverse is possible. The second object of (تنذر) is omitted, i.e. "that you may warn a people of the punishment". Some have allowed (ما) to be a relative, the implied form being "that you may warn a people of the punishment which came to them from a warner before you"; (من نذير) is then attached to (أتاهم), i.e. it came to them on the tongue of a warner before you and through him; so (ما) is a second direct object, for (أنذر) takes two objects — Allah the Exalted said: «فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة». (لعل) and its noun; the clause (يهتدون) is its predicate; and the clause of hope (tarajjī) is a ḥāl from the agent of (لتنذر), i.e. that you may warn them, hoping for their guidance.
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ): (الله) is mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its predicate; the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ما) is conjoined to (السموات); (بينهما) is an adverb attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of (ما); and (في ستة أيام) is attached to (خلق).
(ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا شَفِيعٍ أَفَلا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction of [sequence with] delay; (استوى) is a past verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah; (على العرش) is attached to (استوى). (ما) is negative; (لكم) is a fronted predicate; (من دونه) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (ولي); (من) is a redundant preposition; (ولي) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ; and (ولا شفيع) is conjoined to (ولي). It is also possible, in the view of some grammarians, that (ما) is the Ḥijāzī (ما). The hamza is for the disapproving question; the fāʾ conjoins to something implied that the context requires; (لا) is negative; (تتذكرون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its agent.
(يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّماءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِمَّا تَعُدُّونَ): the clause is circumstantial; (الأمر) is the object of (يدبر); (من السماء) is attached to (يدبر), and (إلى الأرض) is also attached to (يدبر); (من) is for beginning and (إلى) for termination. (ثم) is a conjunction of [sequence with] delay; (يعرج) is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "it", i.e. the affair, i.e. it returns to Him; (إليه) is attached to (يعرج); (في يوم) is a ḥāl from the agent of (يعرج), i.e. being in a day; the clause of (كان), its noun and its predicate is an adjective of (يوم) — further explanation of the meaning of this time will come in the section on rhetoric; (مما) is an adjective of (ألف سنة); and the clause (تعدون) is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
Al-Naḥḥās said: "Day" (al-yawm) in the language means "time"; thus the difficulty that some have raised with the saying of Allah the Exalted in the Sura "Saʾala" [al-Maʿārij], «خمسين ألف سنة» (fifty thousand years), is removed. The Arabs express a period of time with "day"; and the Day of Resurrection contains days of differing durations: some of them are a thousand years in measure and some fifty thousand years in measure. What is meant by mentioning the thousand and the fifty [thousand] is to draw attention to its length and to make one fear it, not the specific number. Among the attestations of expressing a period with "day" is the poet's saying:
يومان: يوم مقامات وأندية ... ويوم سير إلى الأعداء تأويب
(Two days: a day of gatherings and assemblies, and a day of marching against the enemy, travelling all day long.)

dervis-irab:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ): (ذلك) is mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to Allah, the Creator, the Disposer; (عالم الغيب والشهادة) is the first khabar (predicate), (العزيز) the second predicate and (الرحيم) the third predicate.
(الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ): the relative noun may be a fourth predicate, or a naʿt (adjective), or the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ, or it may be accusative by way of praise. The clause (أحسن) is the ṣila (relative clause); (كل شيء) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (خلقه) is a past verb and a direct object, the agent being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form [Translator's note: the source omits the implied form here, reading «تقديره يعود على الله»] referring to Allah; the clause (خلقه) is an adjective of (شيء), in the position of the genitive, or an adjective of (كل), so that it is in the position of the accusative. (خلقه) has also been read with sukūn on the lām (khalqahu), in which case it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from (كل شيء), and the pronoun refers to (كل شيء).
(وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنْسانِ مِنْ طِينٍ): (وبدأ) is conjoined to (أحسن); (خلق الإنسان) is the direct object; (من طين) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلق); and by "man" Adam is meant.
(ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ مِنْ ماءٍ مَهِينٍ): (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay; (جعل نسله) is a verb, a latent agent referring to Allah, and a direct object; (من سلالة) is attached to (جعل), or is in the position of the accusative as a second object. Offspring is called nasl because it slips out (tansilu) from him, just as the sperm-drop is called sulāla because it is drawn out (tusallu) from him. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-najl is offspring (al-nasl); najalahu abūhu means his father begot him; so the child is salīl and najl. (من ماء) is an adjective of (سلالة) and (مهين) an adjective of (ماء), which is the weak sperm-drop.
(ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِهِ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ): (ثم) is a particle of sequence and delay; (سواه) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object, and by "fashioning" (al-taswiya) is meant forming him in the best form. (ونفخ) is conjoined to (سواه); (فيه) is attached to (نفخ), and (من روحه) is also attached to (نفخ); (وجعل) is conjoined; (لكم) is attached to (جعل); (السمع) is the direct object; (الأبصار) and (الأفئدة) are conjoined to (السمع). (قليلا) is mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (ما) is redundant (zāʾida), emphasising the paucity; and (تشكرون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (قليلا) may also be parsed as an adverb of time; on the first the implied form is "a little thanks", and on the second "a little time".
(وَقالُوا أَإِذا ضَلَلْنا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ): resumptive speech, introduced to set out kinds of their falsehoods; the secret of the shift of address (iltifāt) will come in the section on rhetoric [Translator's note: no rhetoric section follows in this entry]. The hamza is for the disapproving question; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, attached to something omitted, its implied form being "we shall be resurrected" — which is the apodosis of (إذا) — or "we shall be brought out", as indicated by (خلق جديد). The clause (ضللنا) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (في الأرض) is attached to (ضللنا). The hamza is again for the disapproving question; (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (في خلق) is its predicate; and (جديد) is an adjective of (خلق).
(بَلْ هُمْ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ كافِرُونَ): a transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī) from setting out their disbelief in the resurrection to what is more calamitous and more indicative of the evil of what they waver in. (هم) is mubtadaʾ; (بلقاء ربهم) is attached to (كافرون); and (كافرون) is the predicate of (هم).
(قُلْ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ الَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ): (يتوفاكم) is an imperfect verb, with the kāf as a fronted direct object; (ملك الموت) is the fāʿil (agent); (الذي) is an adjective of (ملك الموت); the clause (وكل بكم) is the ṣila. (ثم) is a conjunction of [sequence with] delay; (إلى ربكم) is attached to (ترجعون); and (ترجعون) is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Benefits:
The patterns tafaʿʿul and istifʿāl:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-tawaffī is taking the soul in full (istīfāʾ), the soul being the spirit. Allah the Exalted said: «الله يتوفى الأنفس». It is known that tafaʿʿul and istifʿāl meet, as in taqaḍḍaytuhu and istaqḍaytuhu, taʿajjaltuhu and istaʿjaltuhu." Tafaʿʿul has other meanings, which we list below:
1- Being the reflexive-resultative (muṭāwaʿa) of the doubled quadriliteral [i.e. faʿʿala], e.g. nabbahtuhu fa-tanabbaha (I alerted him and he became alert), and jammaʿtuhu fa-tajammaʿa (I gathered it and it gathered together).
2- Affectation, e.g. taṣabbara and takarrama, i.e. he made an effort at patience and generosity.
3- Taking as, e.g. tawassada dhirāʿahu, i.e. he took it as a pillow; and tawarraka al-baʿīr, i.e. he took its haunch as a mount.
4- Avoidance, e.g. taʾaththama, i.e. he avoided sin (ithm); and tahajjada, i.e. he avoided hujūd, which is sleep.
5- Gradualness, e.g. taḥaffaẓtu al-dars, i.e. I memorised the lesson part after part; and tajarraʿtu al-dawāʾ, i.e. I took the medicine gulp after gulp.
The best-known meanings of istifʿāl are the following:
1- Seeking, e.g. istaqdamtu fulānan, i.e. I sought his coming; and istakhrajtu ḥall al-masʾala, i.e. I obtained the solution of the problem after seeking it.
2- Becoming, e.g. istaḥjara, i.e. it became stone; istanwaqa al-jamal, i.e. the he-camel became like a she-camel; and istarjalat al-marʾa, i.e. the woman became like a man.
3- Attribution, e.g. istaṣwabtu raʾyahu, i.e. I attributed correctness to his opinion; and istaqbaḥtu fiʿlahu, i.e. I attributed ugliness to his act.
4- Abbreviation of an utterance, e.g. istarjaʿa al-qawm, i.e. they said: "To Allah we belong and to Him we return."
5- Intensity, e.g. istahtara, i.e. his infatuation became intense; and istakbara, i.e. his arrogance became strong.
This form may come in the sense of afʿala, e.g. istajāba and ajāba (he answered); and it may be its reflexive-resultative, e.g. aḥkamtu al-bināʾ fa-staḥkama (I made the building firm and it became firm), and aqamtu iʿwijājahu fa-staqāma (I straightened its crookedness and it became straight).

dervis-irab:12-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَتَجافى): tajāfā: it moved aside and did not keep to its place. One says: the saddle tajāfā (stood off) from the horse's back, and his side tajāfā from the bed. In al-Asās: "So-and-so jafānī: he did to me what grieved me, and I found him unkind (istajfaytuhu). Literature is a craft whose practitioners are neglected (majfuww). The woman jafat her child: she did not tend it. A jāfin garment: a coarse one, and his garment has become coarse (jafā). He is one of the rude ones (jufāt) of the Arabs. The saddle jafā from the horse's back, and the sleeper's side from the bed, and tajāfā: «تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع». His companion ajfāhu and jāfāhu (kept it away). [The poet] said:
وتشتكي لو أننا نشكيها ... غمز حوايا قلّما نجفيها
(She would complain — if only we would heed her complaint — of the pressing of the saddle-pads, which we seldom lift off her.)
Among the figurative uses: the harshness (jafwa, jafāwa) of time befell him." The jīm together with the fāʾ has the particular sense of contraction and dryness. One says jaffa yajiffu, of the pattern of taʿiba, jafāfan and jufūfan: it became dry and parched — and contraction is clear in this meaning. Ijtaffa mā fī al-ināʾ: he finished what was in the vessel. Jafaʾa yajfaʾu, of the pattern of fataḥa: the river threw up foam and rubbish. Jafjafa al-ibil: he drove the camels hard until some climbed on others, i.e. some contracted upon others. Jafakha: he was arrogant — and the arrogant one draws himself in away from people out of haughtiness and pride. The people jafalū and ajfalū: they fled hastily; and a jafla occurred among the people when they were afraid and so stampeded (injafalū) — and nothing is like the frightened one in contracting and hurrying. Jafana al-nāqa: he slaughtered the she-camel and served its meat in large bowls (jifān); jafana nafsahu: he restrained himself from vile things; tajaffana al-karm: the vine came to have a stock. Al-jafna, with fatḥa on the jīm, is the large bowl, wine, and the small well; so what the common people call "jafnat al-karm" (the grapevine) has a sound basis.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ناكِسُوا رُؤُسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): resumptive speech, introduced to call up the image of the criminals in general on the Day of Resurrection; the address is to Muḥammad ﷺ, or to anyone fit for it, and to embody the horror that has befallen them. (لو) is conditional; (ترى) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (إذ) is an adverb for time past, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترى) — that is permissible only because its occurrence is anticipated and certain, as in «أتى أمر الله»; and Abū al-Baqāʾ made it one of the cases in which (إذ) occupies the place of (إذا). (المجرمون) is mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ناكسو رءوسهم) khabar (predicate) — the secret of the expression with the nominal clause will come in the section on rhetoric. (عند ربهم) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). The object of (ترى) is omitted, because the seeing is visual, i.e. "if you could see the criminals", the mubtadaʾ having made its mention unnecessary. The apodosis of (لو) is omitted, i.e. "you would have seen a horrific matter that cannot be described". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed (لو) to be for wishing (tamannī), with the past sense in it and in (إذ) because what is established in Allah's knowledge is as what has happened. (ناكسو رءوسهم) is an active participle annexed to its object.
(رَبَّنا أَبْصَرْنا وَسَمِعْنا فَارْجِعْنا نَعْمَلْ صالِحاً إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ): the speech is the content of an omitted saying in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "saying". (ربنا) is a vocative (munādā), annexed, from which the vocative particle has been dropped. (أبصرنا) is a verb and its agent, and the object is omitted, i.e. we have seen the truth of Your promise and Your threat, and we have heard from You the confirmation of Your messengers; (وسمعنا) is conjoined to (أبصرنا). It is also possible not to supply an object, i.e. we have become of those who see and hear, whereas before we were deaf and blind — and this is beautiful. (فارجعنا): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; (ارجعنا) is an imperative verb whose purpose is supplication, with a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نعمل) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request; (صالحا) is a direct object or mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and (إنّ), its noun and its predicate.
(وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَآتَيْنا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُداها): the wāw is conjunctive; (لو) is conditional; (شئنا) is a verb and its agent; (لآتينا): the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو), and (آتينا) is a verb and its agent; (كل نفس) is the first object of (آتينا) and (هداها) the second object of (آتينا).
(وَلكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (لكن) is lightened and inoperative, so it is merely for rectification (istidrāk). (حق القول) is a verb and its agent; (مني) is a ḥāl. (لأملأنّ): the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is ordinarily called the lām of the answer to the oath], and (أملأن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its agent latent, its implied form being "I"; (جهنم) is the direct object; (من الجنة) is attached to (أملأن); (الناس) is conjoined to (الجنة). The jinn are mentioned first because the context is one of disparaging them. (أجمعين) is tawkīd (emphasis); the discussion of the meaning of (أجمعين) here will come in the section on benefits.
(فَذُوقُوا بِما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. if you have forgotten all this, then taste. (ذوقوا) is an imperative verb and its agent. (بما): the bāʾ is a preposition of causation and (ما) is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar); the first [Translator's note: so in the source, «الاول»; «المؤول» "interpreted" maṣdar is evidently meant] maṣdar is genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (ذوقوا). The object of (ذوقوا) is omitted, its implied form being "the punishment". (لقاء يومكم) is the object of (نسيتم), and (هذا) is an adjective of (يومكم), i.e. the one referred to.
(إِنَّا نَسِيناكُمْ وَذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْخُلْدِ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): resumptive speech, to increase their pain and to match their forgetting of the meeting with a sharper and more grievous forgetting. (إنّ) and its noun; the clause (نسيناكم) is its predicate. (ذوقوا) is an imperative verb and the wāw is the agent; the clause is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "and We say: taste"; (عذاب الخلد) is the object of (ذوقوا). The tasting is repeated with its object for emphasis and to make clear the object of tasting that had been left unexpressed. (بما) — preposition and its genitive noun — is attached to (ذوقوا), as has just passed. (كنتم): (كان) and its noun; the clause (تعملون) is its predicate.
(إِنَّما يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنَا الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِّرُوا بِها خَرُّوا سُجَّداً): resumptive speech, introduced to describe those who, when the Qur'an is recited to them, fall down prostrating. (إنما) is [a particle] restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (يؤمن) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (بآياتنا) is attached to it; (الذين) is the agent; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (ذكروا) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (بها) is attached to (ذكروا); the clause (خروا) is the apodosis of (إذا); and (سجدا) is a ḥāl from the agent of (خروا).
(وَسَبَّحُوا بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ): (وسبحوا) is conjoined to (خروا); (بحمد ربهم) is a ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يستكبرون) predicate; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
(تَتَجافى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضاجِعِ): the clause is resumptive, or likewise circumstantial; (جنوبهم) is the agent; and (عن المضاجع) is attached to (تتجافى).
(يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ): the clause (يدعون) is either resumptive or likewise circumstantial; (يدعون ربهم) is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object; (خوفا وطمعا) are either mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or two ḥāls, or two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of an omitted verb; (مما) is attached to (ينفقون); and the clause (رزقناهم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما).
(فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the fāʾ may be conjunctive, i.e. their sides forsake [their beds] and they call upon their Lord, so no [soul knows]; and it may be the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. if anyone has hoped [Translator's note: the source reads «إن حلول أحد», which appears corrupt; perhaps «إن حاول أحد» "if anyone has tried"] to know their destiny and the delight of eyes that Allah has prepared for them, then he does not know. (لا) is negative; (تعلم نفس) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (ما) is a relative noun, the object of (تعلم), i.e. it does not know that which Allah has hidden. It may also be interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with (أخفي لهم) its predicate. On the reading (أُخْفِي) with sukūn on the yāʾ, (ما) is the object of (أخفي), because it is an imperfect verb whose agent is "I", and the interrogative (ما) suspends (muʿalliqa) [Translator's note: the source reads «لمتعلم», evidently for «لتعلم»] (تعلم). (لهم) is attached to (أخفي); (من قرة أعين) is a ḥāl from (ما); (جزاء) is an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense", or an object of purpose, i.e. it was hidden for them for the sake of their recompense; (بما) is attached to (جزاء); (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعملون) is its predicate.

* Rhetoric:
Turning from the verbal to the nominal [clause]:
In His saying «ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم» there is a turning from the verbal clause to the nominal clause, to establish their persistence in hanging their heads in shame, embarrassment and disgrace when their faults and misdeeds appear in an ugly, hideous form that provokes mockery and derision of them — as though that continued with them: no head of theirs is raised and no glance of theirs is extended.
Likewise He turned from the verbal to the emphasised nominal [clause] in His saying «إنا موقنون», i.e. they are firm in certainty and desirous of it, after the hidden things [Translator's note: the source reads «المغاب»; «المغيَّبات» or «العواقب» may be meant] have appeared to them, calling down upon them woe and destruction.

* Benefits:
Emphasis with ajmaʿīn:
When it is intended to strengthen the emphasis, it is permissible to follow kullahu with ajmaʿ, kullahā with jamʿāʾ, kulluhum with ajmaʿīn, and kulluhunna with jumaʿ. So you say: "the whole kind came, all of it (kulluhu ajmaʿ)", "the tribe, all of it (kulluhā jamʿāʾ)", "the people, all of them (kulluhum ajmaʿūn)", and "the women, all of them (kulluhunna jumaʿ)". One may emphasise with them even if kull does not precede, as in the previous verse and His saying «لأغوينهم أجمعين».

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ كانَ مُؤْمِناً كَمَنْ كانَ فاسِقاً لا يَسْتَوُونَ): the hamza is for the disapproving question; the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted that the context requires; (من) is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (كان) is the ṣila (relative clause), its noun latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", and (مؤمنا) its khabar (predicate); (كمن) is the predicate of (من); the clause (كان) is the ṣila of the second (من), and (فاسقا) is the predicate of (كان). The clause (لا يستوون) is resumptive, with no place in i'rab; (يستوون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with its fāʿil (agent), and what it is attached to is omitted, i.e. "in the outcome". It is related that he ﷺ used deliberately to pause at His saying (فاسقا) and then begin with His saying (لا يستوون).
Al-Zajjāj said: He made the two a group, saying "they are not equal" (in the plural), because of the meaning of (من); and it has also been said: because two is the minimum plural.
(أَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَلَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ الْمَأْوى نُزُلًا بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) is mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; the clause (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila and enters its domain. (فلهم): the fāʾ is linking, (لهم) is a fronted predicate, and (جنات المأوى) a postponed mubtadaʾ. Al-maʾwā is the place in which one takes refuge; one also says al-maʾwāt and al-maʾwī. (نزلا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (جنات المأوى), i.e. in the state of being prepared and made ready for them. Al-nuzul, with two ḍammas, is the gift for the one who alights (as a guest); then it became general, so its use in the sense of "hotel" (funduq) is unobjectionable — indeed perhaps it is more fitting with respect to high-class hotels, because funduq, on the pattern of qunfudh, is the khān (inn), as in al-Qāmūs, and one also says funtuq. Ibn ʿAbbād said it is the wayside inn, a dialect form of funduq; al-Khafājī rejected it in Shifāʾ al-Ghalīl. The commentator on al-Qāmūs said: "It — i.e. al-Khafājī's statement — is not sound, for al-Farrāʾ said: 'I heard a Bedouin of Quḍāʿa say futuq for funduq, which is the khān.'" (بما) is an adjective of (نزلا); (ما) is maṣdariyya or relative; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعملون) is its predicate.
(وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا فَمَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ): the wāw is conjunctive; (أما) is conditional and detailing, as stated before, and it is usually repeated — a brief reference to it will come in the section on benefits. (الذين) is mubtadaʾ; (فسقوا) is the ṣila; the fāʾ is linking; (مأواهم النار) is a mubtadaʾ and predicate, and the clause is the predicate of (الذين).
(كُلَّما أَرادُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها أُعِيدُوا فِيها وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ ذُوقُوا عَذابَ النَّارِ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ): (كلما) is an adverb of time containing the sense of condition — the discussion of (كلما) has preceded many times. (أرادوا) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is resumptive, to explain the manner of their abode in it; (أن) with what is in its domain is the object of (أرادوا); (منها) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يخرجوا); the clause (أعيدوا) has no grammatical position; (فيها) is attached to (أعيدوا); (وقيل) is conjoined to (أعيدوا), and the wāw [of (أعيدوا)] is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (لهم) is attached to (قيل); the clause (ذوقوا عذاب النار) is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl); (الذي) is an adjective of (العذاب); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila; (به) is attached to (تكذبون); and the clause (تكذبون) is the predicate of (كنتم).
(وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْأَدْنى دُونَ الْعَذابِ الْأَكْبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam) [Translator's note: so in the source]; (نذيقنهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, its agent latent, its implied form being "We", and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من العذاب) — preposition and its genitive noun — is attached to (نذيقنهم); (الأدنى) is an adjective of (العذاب) — by "the nearer" is meant the punishment of this world and the trials and calamities to which they are exposed. (دون) is an adverb of time in the sense of "before", attached to an omitted ḥāl; (العذاب) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (الأكبر) is an adjective — by "the greater" is meant the punishment of the Hereafter. (لعل), its noun and its predicate; the clause of hope (tarajjī) is circumstantial, and by it is meant the hope of those addressed, as Sībawayh said in explaining it.
(وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآياتِ رَبِّهِ ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْها إِنَّا مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُنْتَقِمُونَ): resumptive speech, introduced to show the state of one who meets the favour with turning away and averting [his face] from it. (من) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, mubtadaʾ; (أظلم) is predicate; (ممن) is attached to (أظلم); the clause (ذكر) is the ṣila of (من); (بآيات ربه) is attached to (ذكر); (ثم) is a conjunction of [sequence with] delay; (أعرض) is conjoined to (ذكر); (عنها) is attached to (أعرض) — the meaning of the delay will come in the section on rhetoric. (إنا): (إنّ) and its noun; (من المجرمين) is attached to (منتقمون); and (منتقمون) is the predicate of (إنّ).

* Rhetoric:
1- We mentioned earlier that the conjunctions have secrets that only the discerning grasp, so it is not correct to put some in place of others because of the differences between them. The word «ثم» is particular to [expressing] remoteness [of likelihood] and lengthiness of duration, and its mention was fitting in His saying «ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها», because turning away from the signs, with their utmost clarity and radiance, is considered remote by the judgement of established self-evident truth and the scales of sound minds. The poets have gazed at the sky of this eloquence; Jaʿfar ibn ʿUlba al-Ḥārithī said, in what the Dīwān al-Ḥamāsa relates:
ولا يكشف الغمّاء إلا ابن حرّة ... يرى غمرات الموت ثم يزورها
نقاسمهم أسيافنا شر قسمة ... ففينا غواشيها وفيهم صدورها
(None removes the overwhelming calamity but the son of a free woman, who sees the floods of death and then visits them. We share our swords with them in the worst of sharing: in us are their coverings (hilts), and in them their fronts (blades).)
He likened the overwhelming calamity to a concrete thing that covers people and overspreads them, by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). He said "the son of a free woman" to spur the listener and rouse him to plunge into battle. The "floods of death" are its hardships and terrors. The point of evidence is in his saying "and then visits them": he considered it remote that one should visit the floods of death after seeing them and being certain of them, because between seeing frightening terrors and descending into them with a desire resembling the desire to meet the beloved there is, by custom and reason, a great distance. He likened the swords, extended and lying between them, to a thing in which sharing takes place, by way of implicit metaphor; then he derived from that sharing that they have the coverings, i.e. what covers them of the swords, which are the hilts — or because these extend beyond the blade, so they cover it — while their enemies have their fronts, i.e. their leading ends, the front (ṣadr) of anything being its foremost part. He expressed it with "in" (fī) rather than the lām because «في» conveys only the enemies' containing the fronts, since they enter their bodies, whereas the lām conveys ownership, which is not intended — even if it is what sharing would require — so perhaps he warded off that notion by turning to «في», and mentioned it first as a preparation for the second.
2- In His saying «وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار» to the end of the verse there is one of the devices of badīʿ (embellishment) that none of those who wrote on the devices of badīʿ mentioned except Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ, namely al-shamāta (gloating): mentioning the misfortunes and trials that have befallen your enemy as recompense for what his hands have earned, together with exaggeration in depicting his distress and the terrors in which he flounders, and showing your delight at what has befallen him, in gloating over him and taking satisfaction from him. In this verse there are kinds of satisfaction and gloating that are not hidden. It is widespread in the Qur'an and in poetry; among it is the ode "Fatḥ al-Futūḥ" (the Conquest of Conquests) of Abū Tammām.

* Benefits:
A return to ammā:
(أَمَّا), with fatḥa on the hamza and doubling of the mīm, is a particle of condition, emphasis and, usually, detailing. The meaning of condition is indicated by the fāʾ usually coming after it; the meaning of detailing is indicated by the survey of its occurrences and by the conjoining of another like it to it. It must have a fāʾ following what follows it, unless the fāʾ enters upon a [verb of] saying that has been dropped, the content of the saying making it unnecessary, in which case it must be omitted along with it.

dervis-irab:23-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْجُرُزِ): one says: time jarazahu: it swept him away. Tubbaʿ said:
لا تسقني بيديك إن لم ألقها ... جرزا كأن أشاءها مجروز
(Do not give me drink with your hands if I do not find it [the land] bare, as though its young palms had been cut down.)
A majrūza land, and it has been jurizat: its vegetation has been cut off; a juruz land, ajrāz lands; ajrāz years: barren years; and a mijrāz desert. Al-Rāʿī said:
وغبراء مجراز يبيت دليلها ... مشيحا عليها للفراقد راعيا
(And many a dusty, barren desert whose guide spends the night wary upon it, watching the Farqad stars.)
A jurāz sword [i.e. a sharp, cutting one]; and "A hater will not be satisfied except with a jarza" is a proverb about enmity: that the one who hates is satisfied only with the uprooting of the one he hates and his being struck with the jurz (club). They went out with jarazāt in their hands; and he brought a jurza of qatt (fodder), and a jurz of it — that is the bundle. The common people use this word a great deal, and it is unobjectionable, as you see. Among the figurative uses: a jarūz man: a big eater who leaves nothing on the table; and a jāriz woman: a barren one. In al-Mukhtār: "A juruz and a jurz land, like ʿusr, is one without vegetation", i.e. it has been cut off and removed entirely; and it has been said that it is the name of a place in Yemen. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-jurza: the handful of qatt and the like, or the bundle; the plural is juraz, like ghurfa and ghuraf. A juruz land, with two ḍammas, is one from which the water has been cut off, so it is dry with no vegetation in it."

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ فَلا تَكُنْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقائِهِ): resumptive speech, introduced to console him ﷺ. Moses was chosen only because the Jews and Christians believed in him, so He held to what is agreed upon so that it would be more binding in establishing the argument against them. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (آتينا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (موسى) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (آتينا) and (الكتاب) the second direct object. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; (لا) is prohibitive; (تكن) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you"; (في مرية) is its khabar (predicate), i.e. doubt; (من لقائه) is an adjective of (مرية). The pronoun in (لقائه) refers to Moses, so the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely (لقاء), is annexed to its object; or to the Book, in which case the annexation is to the agent, i.e. of the Book's meeting Moses. There are many views on the reference of the pronoun which we have passed over because of their incoherence.
(وَجَعَلْناهُ هُدىً لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): (جعلناه) is a verb, agent and direct object, the pronoun referring to Moses, and to the Book as well; (هدى) is the second direct object; and (لبني إسرائيل) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (هدى) or is an adjective of it.
(وَجَعَلْنا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا وَكانُوا بِآياتِنا يُوقِنُونَ): (وجعلنا) is conjoined to the first (جعلنا); (منهم) is the second object of (جعلنا) and (أئمة) the first object of (جعلنا); the clause (يهدون) is an adjective of (أئمة); (بأمرنا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (لما) is an adverb in the sense of "when", attached to (جعلنا), i.e. We made them leaders when they were patient. The apodosis of (لما) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, the implied form being "and when they were patient We made from among them leaders". (وكانوا) is conjoined to (صبروا); (بآياتنا) is attached to (يوقنون); and (يوقنون) is the predicate of (كانوا).
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فِيما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ): (إنّ) and its noun; (هو) is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يفصل) is the predicate of (إنّ), or the predicate of (هو) with the clause being the predicate of (إنّ); (بينهم) is an adverb attached to (يفصل); (يوم القيامة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (فيما) is attached to (يفصل); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون); and the clause (يختلفون) is the predicate of (كانوا).
(أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِي مَساكِنِهِمْ): the hamza is for the disapproving question; the wāw conjoins to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Have they been heedless, and has it not guided them", i.e. become clear. (لم) is a particle of negation, transformation [of tense] and the jussive; (يهد) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. The agent is what «لم يهد» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably what «كم أهلكنا» indicates is meant] indicates, because (كم) does not occur as an agent; the implied form is "Has not the multitude of Our destroying the generations guided them?" — and you may take this speech itself as the implied form. (كم) is the declarative (khabariyya) one, in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of (أهلكنا); (من قبلهم) is a ḥāl from (القرون), and (من القرون) is likewise a ḥāl from (كم). The clause (يمشون) is either resumptive, introduced to show how they are guided, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in (لهم), the implied sense being: they walk, i.e. pass in their travels for trade by their dwellings and lands, and see the traces of their destruction; (في مساكنهم) is attached to (يمشون).
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ أَفَلا يَسْمَعُونَ): (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted predicate; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (آيات) is the postponed noun of (إنّ). The hamza is for the disapproving question; the fāʾ conjoins to something implied that the style of the speech requires, i.e. "Have they become deaf, so they do not hear?"; (لا) is negative; and (يسمعون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَسُوقُ الْماءَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ): the hamza is for the disapproving question; the wāw likewise conjoins to something implied; (لم) is a particle of negation, transformation and the jussive; (يروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم), and the wāw is the agent; (أنّ) with what is in its domain stands in place of the object of (يروا); (أنّ) and its noun; the clause (نسوق) is its predicate; (الماء) is the direct object; (إلى الأرض) is attached to (نسوق); and (الجرز) is an adjective (naʿt) of (الأرض).
(فَنُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعاً تَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ أَنْعامُهُمْ وَأَنْفُسُهُمْ أَفَلا يُبْصِرُونَ): (فنخرج) is conjoined to (نسوق); the agent of (نخرج) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; (به) is attached to (نخرج); (زرعا) is the direct object; the clause (تأكل) is an adjective of (زرعا); (منه) is attached to (تأكل); (أنعامهم) is the agent of (تأكل); (أنفسهم) is conjoined to (أنعامهم). The hamza is for the disapproving question; the i'rab of the like of (فلا يبصرون) has preceded.
(وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْفَتْحُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): resumptive speech, introduced to answer their mockery; for they used to ridicule the Muslims who said, "Allah will grant us victory over the polytheists and judge between us and them", and they would say: "When is this victory?" (متى) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted predicate; (هذا) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (الفتح) is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم): (كان) and its noun, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (صادقين) is the predicate of (كان); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
(قُلْ يَوْمَ الْفَتْحِ لا يَنْفَعُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِيمانُهُمْ وَلا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ): (يوم الفتح) is mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, though (يومَ) is accusative in the verse; it is ordinarily parsed as an adverb attached to (ينفع)] and the clause (لا ينفع) its predicate; (الذين كفروا) is the fronted object of (ينفع) and (إيمانهم) the postponed agent of (ينفع). The wāw is conjunctive; (هم) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (ينظرون) predicate; (ينظرون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. they are given respite.
(فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَانْتَظِرْ إِنَّهُمْ مُنْتَظِرُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; (أعرض) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (عنهم) is attached to (أعرض); (انتظر) is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", and its object is omitted, its implied form being "victory over them". (إنّ) and its noun; (منتظرون) is its predicate; and the object of (منتظرون), which is an active participle, is likewise omitted, its implied form being "victory over you".

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «أو لم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم» to the end of the verse, there is the device of al-munāsaba (correspondence). Correspondence is of two divisions: correspondence in meanings or correspondence in words. The first is that the speaker begins with a meaning and then completes his speech with what corresponds to it in meaning, not in wording. Examples of it have passed in al-Anʿām and al-Qaṣaṣ, and in this verse: at its beginning Allah the Exalted said "Has it not guided them", which is an audible admonition, since they had not looked at the destroyed generations but had only heard of them; so it was fitting that He should bring after it His saying «أفلا يسمعون» (Will they not then hear?). As for after the visible admonition, which is His saying «أو لم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز», it was fitting that He should say «أفلا يبصرون» (Will they not then see?), because crops are seen, not heard — so that the end of each speech corresponds to its beginning.
As for verbal correspondence, it is bringing words of equal measure, rhymed and unrhymed. The rhymed with equal measure is complete correspondence, and the unrhymed with equal measure is incomplete correspondence. The latter is more widespread in eloquent speech, because of the absence of affectation and because rhyme is not required in it; if it occurs incorporated into the speech without affectation, it is acceptable and is a marvel of beauty. Its examples in the Noble Qur'an will come, and an example of it preceded in His saying in Yūnus: «لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم». Among the attestations of the complete [kind] in the ḥadīth is his saying ﷺ, in what is related from him of the supplication with which he used to seek protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah (al-tāmma), from every devil and venomous creature (hāmma), and from every evil eye (ʿayn lāmma)." He did not say mulimma, which is the regular form, because of the correspondence. Among what has come of complete verbal correspondence is the saying of Ibn Hāniʾ al-Andalusī, from some verses:
وعوانس وقوانس وفوارس ... وكوانس وأوانس وعقائل
(Unmarried maidens, helmet-crests and horsemen; [gazelles] in their lairs, sociable ladies and noble women.)
And of incomplete verbal correspondence:
مها الوحش إلا أن هاتا أوانس ... قنا الحظ إلا أن تلك ذوابل
(Wild oryx — except that these are sociable; spears of al-Khaṭṭ — except that those are withered.) [Translator's note: the source prints «قنا الحظ»; the well-known verse reads «قنا الخطّ», the spears of al-Khaṭṭ.]
He made an incomplete correspondence between mahā and qanā, between al-waḥsh and al-ḥaẓẓ [al-khaṭṭ], and between awānis and dhawābil.
